title: mentha arvensis subsp. parietariifolia
intro: Mentha arvensis subsp. parietariifolia, commonly known as Japanese wild mint, is a subspecies of the mint plant that is native to East Asia. This plant is known for its numerous health benefits, including its ability to alleviate digestive issues, reduce inflammation, and act as an antiseptic, making it a valuable herb in traditional medicine. The therapeutic actions of Japanese wild mint include its anti-spasmodic, anti-inflammatory, and antiseptic properties, which contribute to its use in treating a range of health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Japanese wild mint include menthone, limonene, and rosmarinic acid, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
